 Govt may extend flood aid to small traders, says Zahid
 Friday, 20 Nov 2026
 share 
 bookmark 
 KUALA LUMPUR: A proposal to extend flood aid to affected small traders will be brought to the Central Disaster Management Committee for consideration, says Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi (pic).
 The Deputy Prime Minister said the government is considering extending flood aid for small tra­ders.
 “Currently, the Bantuan Wang Ihsan (compassionate cash aid) is disbursed to flood victims before they return home.
 “That means while they are still at the flood relief centres (PPS), we try our best to give it to them then.
 “We will also provide aid to those who do not evacuate to a PPS but are affected, as long as they are regis­tered at the flood victim registration centre,” he said, responding to a supplementary question from Tampin MP Datuk Mohd Isam Mohd Isa.
 Separately, Ahmad Zahid said at least 159 NGOs nationwide are on standby to assist flood victims during the ongoing north-east monsoon season.
 “Non-uniformed NGOs are coordinated by the Welfare Department under the disaster management framework. ... Coordination has been carried out at all levels, including with NGOs mobilised by political parties, regardless of political affiliation,” he said.
 Ahmad Zahid also said more than 100,000 personnel from response and technical agencies have been mobilised for the monsoon, along with support from various assets and operational equipment.
 “Among them are nearly 2,500 boats, more than 2,000 four-wheel-drive vehicles, more than 1,100 lorries, 28 aircraft and over 35,000 safety life jackets, including 101 assets from the Public Works Department on standby,” he said.
 Ahmad Zahid said they have identified 3,045 flood hotspots and have also looked at 31 landslide hotspot areas.
 “At least 90 are categorised as high critical, 92 as medium critical and 81 as low critical,” he added.
